lines: This was a church in a foreign land.
Still, churches have nothing to do with foreign or home countries. All that was here was prayer and serenity...
...or so it should have been.
DADADADADADADAAA!!!
Thug A
Hey hey, you stinky monks! If you don’t want to die, get that damn nun out of here right now!
Thug B
I’ll take you to the real heaven with my prized pistol! Gahaha!
Suddenly, a group of nasty-looking men burst into the church.
They waved their guns around, spraying bullets everywhere to intimidate.
The reason they forced their way in was… a grudge.
They were a gang that ruled the neighboring town and were plotting to expand into this city.
A few days earlier, as a preliminary move, a handful of their underlings roamed the streets and caused a ruckus in a cheap tavern for fun.
Naturally, a clash broke out with those who didn’t like the newcomers making a scene…
And the opponent turned out to be a young beautiful woman dressed in a nun’s habit.
Moreover, that woman was as drunk, if not more, than the thugs.
She was beaten senseless by the drunken woman, unable to fight back, and barely escaped with her life.
The underlings made excuses, saying they’d let their guard down because they thought she was a woman… and were promptly dealt with.
With such rumors spreading, they realized they couldn’t even control the local area, let alone expand into new territory.
So they sent the whole gang to the town, coming to settle the debt from that day.
Thug A
What’s up? Nobody’s coming out… is Vivi scared?
The thugs rampaged through the church, breaking things as a show of force.
Then a man burst in through the church’s entrance.
Guide
Hey, hey! What are you guys doing? I never heard about doing something like this!
He was the town guide hired out of necessity after the underlings killed a patrol while scouting the city.
Guide
Get out right now! Don't you realize who you're picking a fight with!
Thug B
Huh, what's this? Are you some kind of worshipper? You wanna be punished? If you think there's divine retribution, go ahead and bring it on!
Guide
That's not it! Damn it! Do you really think this place is just a church!?
Thug A
Huh?
Guide
There are many things you shouldn't mess with in this town! This is one of them, commonly called the "Violence Church"—
Just as the guide hurried to warn them,
Heh, so you really want divine punishment, huh?
Thugs
Gah!
In stark contrast to the thugs' noisy gunfire, there were only three gunshots. And three screams.
With a practiced click, she swapped magazines and lumbered out from behind the altar—a lone nun.
Want me to tell you what's written in this gospel? Anyone who disturbs my nap gets killed—"Kill Them All"!
Thug A
You!
The thugs were momentarily stunned by her dazzling gunplay.
But they weren't just wooden puppets; they instantly raised their guns and took aim.
Shut up... you damn idiots. Your trigger pull is too slow! Like a worn‑out whore's... you know.
The nun leapt, gripping the back of a pew, as bullets whizzed past her.
Floating in the air, she methodically shot the thugs one by one.
Guide
Aaaah!
Realizing he couldn't survive, the guide scrambled away, rolling as he fled.
Ugh, what a goddamn Jesus Christ. We'll make sure to take proper revenge on anyone who messed with Rosarita Cisneros’s blissful moment!
Her nun's skirt fluttered as she landed lightly like an angel.
She flashed a devilish grin and swapped magazines again.
Director
Cut!!! ...Wow, okay!
Me
Phew, that was something...
I pulled myself up from the blood‑splattered floor where I had collapsed.
I was badly wounded, but no need to worry. It was all a fake made of props and fake blood.
――Right, everything that just happened was a movie shoot. I was just one of the thugs in it, a background extra.
The lead actress kept flubbing her lines, so the shoot dragged on, but we finally got an OK take.
That lead actress was none other than Taimanin Shinganji Kurenai.
Kurenai, who met me through a New Year’s mission, is cooperating on a pilot version of a film at the request of director UCOA.
The film is a B‑movie based on a CIA agent the director claimed to have researched in Southeast Asia.
According to the director, everything except the actors is almost nonfiction, and they chose a location with a climate similar to the setting. That’s the pitch, anyway…
The nun is a heavy drinker with a quick temper, and the church is called the “Violence Church,” but behind the scenes she’s a top‑class CIA operative, all acting.
It’s so over‑the‑top it feels like pure fiction. Probably the events are real, just compiled from several people’s episodes… something like that.
By the way, a pilot version is a test film made to attract sponsors.
Anyway, Kurenai is indeed the star, but they can’t afford to hire actors, so she isn’t debuting as an actress.
Honestly, her looks and figure could pass for a real actress, I won’t deny that…
Shinganji Kurenai
“Good work. Here, I got your change of clothes.”
At that moment, Kurenai, still dressed like that nun, rushed over.
Me
“Ah, sorry… I didn’t mean to make the lead actress carry a mob’s costume.”
Shinganji Kurenai
“Huh, what are you talking about? If you’re a celebrity it’s one thing, but in your real role—”
Shinganji Kurenai
“Besides, I was the one who asked you to come along and put yourself through this…”
Right, I’m here because Kurenai asked me to.
To be precise, I was persuaded by Ayame and Asuka, who were worried about her boasting she could do it alone, to accompany her.
By the way, they were frustrated that they couldn't join the mission because they were so busy.
Me
Is the next scene's shoot okay? That's the end of my part...
Shinganji Kurenai
Yeah, it looks like we'll be taking a break for a while. So, um, after you change...
Shinganji Kurenai
Want to wander around that area together?
Shinganji Kurenai
Phew, the wind feels great. It's different from both UCOA and Japan... somehow refreshing.
After browsing the nearby souvenir stalls and street vendors, we sat side by side at an outdoor table set up at a drink shop.
Kurenai was still in her sister outfit because she had another shoot.
Still, she had left her prop sunglasses and gun behind, so she looked like an ordinary sister you could see anywhere.
Shinganji Kurenai
Still… Fuuma is amazing.
Me
…Huh, what?
When the words came out after a brief pause, I was confused because they sounded like praise I hadn't earned.
Shinganji Kurenai
Even though it was a sudden request to appear, you adapted to the shoot so quickly, and your thug acting—completely opposite to your personality—was spot on.
Me
No, no, I barely had any lines and I was stumbling over them, shaking with nerves.
Shinganji Kurenai
That's what makes it feel natural. It's like facing death and still reaching out to someone you shouldn't.
Me
I‑I see...
Shinganji Kurenai
Exactly!
Maybe it's a sense of duty to the main plot; Kurenai would occasionally lift me up like this, and once it starts, it doesn't easily stop.
So I casually changed the subject.
Me
Anyway, why did you take on this shoot, Kurenai?
The female lead of this movie is, well, free‑spirited, lively, self‑indulgent, stiff, clumsy, and hates standing out—basically the opposite of Kurenai.
Of course, the director liked Kurenai enough to personally cast her.
I thought that the usual Kurenai would politely decline and recommend someone like Asuka, who fits the character better.
Shinganji Kurenai
Yeah... actually, I was thinking of turning it down.
Shinganji Kurenai
But after the director watched it and I read the pilot script he gave me, I ended up liking it.
Me
The script?
Shinganji Kurenai
Yeah... well, to be precise, it's about the woman I'm playing right now.
Saying that, Kurenai took a sip of her juice.
Shinganji Kurenai
This lead character is a wild girl who drinks alcohol and shoots guns while wearing a nun's habit...
Shinganji Kurenai
But she's not just that. That's only one side of her. Her true identity is an agent sent from UCOA.
Shinganji Kurenai
Even though she understands that corruption is creeping into her country and organization, she sticks to her mission in her own way.
Shinganji Kurenai
She's such a tough, cool woman that I'm really interested in her. I want to become a woman like that, too.
Shinganji Kurenai
...That's why I took on this shoot.
Me
Uh, yeah...
After Kurenai finished speaking in one breath, that was all I could answer.
I thought the lead does have those traits, but I wondered if it really went that far.
Maybe I’m idealizing it a bit too much because I liked it so much.
Somehow her reckless habit feels familiar to me.
Me
Well... if you liked it that much, you should stop spamming NGs soon.
Shinganji Kurenai
At my words, Kurenai averted her eyes. Indeed, her acting is stricter than mine, and because she's the lead, it caused the NGs.
The action scenes are fine, but her regular acting—especially long lines—was disastrous.
Shinganji Kurenai
Um, it's just that... the way she uses those words, the phrasing, is...
Kurenai hesitated. That way of speaking would make anyone hesitate, not just her.
Shinganji Kurenai
N-no, but the criticism is spot on. And thinking about it, she deliberately used that diction in her performance...
Shinganji Kurenai
Ugh, yeah! That's right, I have to work hard too...!
But as expected of Kurenai, she rallied herself and got fired up.
Me
Then until the break is over, shall we do a script read‑through together?
Me
If we do that, the next scene might go well, right?
I wanted to be that kind of support for Kurenai, so I made a suggestion.
Shinganji Kurenai
Ah! That's right! Will you hang out with me, Fuuma, thanks!
Then Kurenai broke into a beaming smile and was delighted.
